speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, please describe when these symptoms first started and if they are progressive or intermittent. Have you noticed any associated issues with your vision, speech, or coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the "drunk" appearance and clumsiness on the right side suggest cerebellar involvement. To help localize the lesion, could you tell me if you have noticed any slurred speech, double vision, or tremors when you reach for objects?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; given your history of Crohn's disease and the use of natalizumab, we must urgently evaluate your risk for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES. Do you have any recent visual disturbances or changes in your cognitive function?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature Normothermic, Blood Pressure Within normal range, Heart Rate Within normal range, Respiratory Rate Within normal range. Neurological Examination: Gait Assessment Ataxic gait noted, Right Upper Limb Strength 4/5, Coordination Tests Evidence of ataxia. MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML); Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease. The MRI findings of non-enhancing multifocal demyelinating lesions in the context of natalizumab use are pathognomonic. No further questions are required; immediate cessation of natalizumab and initiation of immunomodulatory therapy is indicated.
